summary: Auth token swap during control-plane fallback causes elevated p50/p95 and 401-retry patterns
environment: prod | eu-west -> us-east (tenant uses dedicated eu-west pool)
description: Issue summary: After customer toggled strict-region routing for their tenant, production traffic for the tenant started showing intermittent latency spikes (p50 up by ~60ms, p95 up by ~400ms) and a pattern of 401 -> token refresh -> retry which increases tail latency. Impact: user-facing inference requests (chat streaming and short completion calls) have higher failure rate and slower perceived response for end users. Environment: Dedicated tenant running in eu-west with control-plane pin set to strict-region; some requests observed to be routed to a secondary us-east edge during short control-plane refresh windows. Expected: strict-region should prefer local eu-west edge and not cause auth re-negotiation or cross-region token churn. Actual: during control-plane pin refresh the edge routing flips briefly to a secondary edge which triggers token rotation and auth cache misses leading to additional TLS handshakes and request retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant has strict-region routing enabled and is pinned to eu-west dedicated pool
2) Trigger a config refresh (simulate by toggling and re-enabling strict-region in console or via API),
3) Send a burst of streaming requests from client SDK that reuses a token scoped to the tenant
4) Observe a subset of requests route to us-east edge, see auth 401s and SDK churn / retries, and increased latency on those requests
logs: 2026-03-10T09:12:03Z edge-proxy[eid:edge-8792] WARN request_id=rx-9f2a auth: token validation failed: token-residency-mismatch
2026-03-10T09:12:03Z auth-service[svc-3] INFO token-swap: issued new token for tenant=fin50; issued_at=2026-03-10T09:12:03Z ttl=300s
2026-03-10T09:12:03Z edge-proxy[eid:edge-2911] INFO routing: selected secondary_edge=us-east-1 for tenant fin50 due to pin-refresh-window
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: control-plane's pin refresh window is misaligned with token TTL leading to tokens that encode residency claims no longer matching selected edge during transient routing change.
Observed token change events correlate exactly with times of elevated p50/p95 and with edge selection logs showing temporary selection of us-east edge.
Auth service currently uses short token TTL (5 minutes) and token contains a residency stamp which is validated by the edge. When edge changes, validation fails and edge asks client to refresh.
SDK behaviour: client SDK retries on 401 by fetching a new token and reissuing the request. This is correct but adds extra round-trips if the edge flip happens mid-request.
We confirmed the issue reproduces in a controlled test where we force a pin refresh and stream 50 concurrent requests: ~12% show auth retry path and higher latencies.
No indication of model-serving timeouts or GPU shortage; CPU and GPU metrics on dedicated pool are normal during windows.
Network traces show additional TLS handshakes (full) for the affected requests indicating connection teardown between client and selected edge during the transition window.
comments: Customer (Elena Petrova): We're seeing intermittent user-facing delay spikes and some requests fail with authentication errors right after we change residency policies. Is there a recommended workaround?
Support (Maria Chen): Thanks Elena — we've started an investigation. Can you confirm if your SDK is using token refresh on 401s? Also, do you have a reproducible script to simulate the policy toggle?
Customer (Elena Petrova): Yes the SDK refreshes on 401. We can provide a replay script that toggles the tenant pin every 30s. Will attach privately.

SRE (Olivia Park): We've reproduced with the provided script. Evidence points to a race between control-plane pin rotation and token TTL. Short-term mitigation: we can temporarily increase token TTL or stagger pin refresh to avoid flips during heavy client streams.

Support (Diego Alvarez): Applied mitigation for tenant fin50: increased pin-refresh-stagger to 5s and set control-plane to prefer same-edge for 30s post-refresh. Observed reduction in retries during a 30-minute test window.
Customer (Elena Petrova): After your mitigation we've seen p50 drop back to baseline and no 401s in the last 45 minutes. Thanks. Will keep monitoring from our side.
SRE (Olivia Park): Creating follow-up internal tasks to address root cause: change token/residency contract so tokens are valid across brief edge handoffs and align refresh window with token TTL.
resolution: Mitigation applied: pin-refresh-stagger increased for tenant fin50 and control-plane set to prefer sticky-edge for 30s post-refresh. Observed immediate reduction in auth retries and p50/p95 improved in customer tests. Next steps: SRE to implement a control-plane patch to add continuity headers during edge handoff and update token policy so tokens tolerate micro-handoffs. Follow-up internal story created (INT-570) to change default token TTL and add unit tests for handoff window. Customer monitoring to continue; we'll follow up with a post-incident note.
next_steps: SRE: implement edge continuity header and ensure token validation tolerates short residence mismatch (INT-570)
SRE: increase default token TTL from 300s to 600s for dedicated tenants as an interim safety measure
Engineering: add e2e test that simulates pin refresh during streaming workload
Support: schedule a 1:1 review with FinSight SRE in 48 hours to confirm stability
